stories.title: Ollama + Anthropic Direct + OpenRouter Provider Priority
acceptanceCriteria: AC0 (Security): ACM pipeline reads API keys ONLY from ACM_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and ACM_OPENROUTER_API_KEY env vars (or DB model.api_key field). The bare ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and OPENAI_API_KEY env vars must NOT be read by any ACM extraction code path — these are reserved for Claude Code host tooling.

AC1 (Priority order): Provider selection follows: 1) Ollama (if OLLAMA_API_BASE set) → 2) Anthropic direct (if ACM_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY set or DB key present) → 3) OpenRouter (if ACM_OPENROUTER_API_KEY set or DB key present). First available wins.
AC2 (Ollama primary): When OLLAMA_API_BASE is configured, Ollama qwen2.5:7b is always tried first before any cloud provider.
AC3 (Anthropic direct): ChatAnthropic client instantiated with api_key from ACM_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY env var or model.api_key field — never from the bare ANTHROPIC_API_KEY env var.
AC4 (OpenRouter fallback): OpenRouter used only when both Ollama and Anthropic direct are unavailable or fail auth. Key from ACM_OPENROUTER_API_KEY or DB.
AC5 (DB key storage): model table supports optional api_key field. If set, it takes precedence over env var for that provider. API endpoint PATCH /api/models/{id} allows setting/updating the key.
AC6 (No env bleed): uv run pytest tests/test_openrouter_provider_routing.py confirms no bare ANTHROPIC_API_KEY/OPENAI_API_KEY reads in extraction code path.
AC7: _provision_fallback_model() in open_notebook/graphs/utils.py updated to use new priority order and ACM-namespaced env vars.
AC8: Broadmeadows 31/31 accuracy maintained; Alexander >=40/43 baseline.
